boundary_selection.reason: equal qualified-domain coverage and component-wise relative support on the preregistered common cohort

rl1.qualification_note: The strict every-adjacent-step monotonicity gate fails because very small residual differences occur after the error curve reaches its Reference/time-level plateau. This does not reverse the strong coarse-to-fine convergence evidence.
rl1.residual_plateau_interpretation: R12 and R16 are effectively on the same integrated-error floor. Residual differences may contain Reference SWKIMPL=0 time-level and balance-materialized exchange semantics in addition to LARE spatial/integration error; no zero-asymptote claim is made.

scientific_interpretation: The fixed-domain arbitrary prescribed-head problem no longer requires a fitted boundary coefficient.
CURRENT_LAYER_FACE is the supported no-fit boundary closure for subsequent fixed-domain LARE research.
Aggressive low dimension remains limited mainly by internal gradient reconstruction and spatial closure resolution, not by the bottom-face conductivity choice.
Moving-water-table geometry is not covered by BC1 because the unsaturated control volume itself changes with H(t).
BC1 does not establish an application-independent acceptable dimension or a computational-value claim.

An R16 attribution control shows that importing the Reference SWKIMPL=0 lower-face conductivity time level does not remove the residual plateau; it improves instantaneous flux slightly while worsening cumulative exchange and maximum storage. The residual therefore cannot be assigned primarily to lower-face K timing.

stage_d.interpretation: Observation-lagged lower-face K is not a dominant explanation of the R16 plateau and remains diagnostic only; CURRENT_LAYER_FACE remains the supported physical closure.
